title: satellite-scale reconciliation (90d vs 180d, screen vs sample)

screens.repaired: jump-repair: |dr-med|>30*MAD flagged diffs replaced by median drift, >12 flagged -> discard
screens.legacy: reconstructed all-or-nothing: ANY |dr|>30*MAD (drift-inclusive) -> entire satellite-day discarded

interpretation: On identical preprocessing the fitted exponential scale is NOT stable across the corpus: step_36's 90 days reproduce 14,911 km exactly, the first 90 days of step_98's corpus (different days, same estimator) return 14,835 +/- 1,013 km -- statistically identical -- while the second 90 days return an unresolved fit (lambda at the grid edge, R2=0.661, contrast +0.313, log_slope -0.188) and the pooled 180-day fit gives 8,140 +/- 795 km.  The binned curve flattens beyond ~29 Mm, so lambda and the C0 pedestal trade off and the scale estimate is ill-conditioned on any single window; the contrast (+0.30) and log-slope (-0.17 to -0.19) are stable across every subset and are the robust observables.  The reconstructed legacy all-or-nothing screen on the SAME 90 days retains only 7,449 pair-days versus 74,358 (-58% satellite-days) and degrades the fit to 13,028 +/- 3,274 km (sigma tripled): the screen repair is validated, and the 14,911 vs 8,140 km difference is a finite-corpus conditioning effect on a weakly-constrained tail fit, not a screen artefact.  The 180-day pooled fit is the authoritative value.
